title: Production only changes via an explicit promote step; no upload path auto-promotes
description: Production traffic serving is a distinct action from uploading a version. No CI path may take an uploaded version and route production traffic to it as a side effect of the upload. Production only changes when a Promote step runs and names the version id to serve. The promote step is authored as a separate CI workflow triggered by explicit operator action (`workflow_dispatch` on GitHub Actions or the equivalent manual-trigger primitive on other CI platforms). The promote workflow accepts one input: `versionId` (empty defaults to the newest-of-main resolved from the preview alias); every promote emits a structured record naming the version id promoted, the operator principal that triggered the workflow, the previously-serving version id, and the timestamp.
rationale: The failure mode this ends: a merge lands, the CI pipeline deploys straight to production, and nobody notices the bad release until the phone rings. Decoupling upload from promote makes the ship-to-production act a first-class human decision. The default of newest-of-main keeps the promote fast for the common case; the explicit versionId keeps rollback and hotfix promotes on the same code path.
